policy: A cited occurrence demonstrates a written form in one source, not automatic verification of its grammatical classification. ENL Coyoacan records are mid-sixteenth-century; the Gospel of Luke (1833) reflects nineteenth-century Puebla-area Nahuatl. Period and dialect must remain explicit.

sources.name: Digital Florentine Codex
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute / Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana
sources.kind: Primary historical manuscript / critical digital edition
sources.rights: Manuscript images CC BY-NC-ND; Anderson–Dibble Nahuatl transcriptions and translations used by permission; rights reserved. Links and brief identifying excerpts only.
sources.note: A linked folio is evidence for the spelling on that folio, not automatic confirmation of its part of speech, meaning, animacy or morphology.

sources.name: Online Nahuatl Dictionary
sources.publisher: Stephanie Wood, ed.; Wired Humanities Projects, University of Oregon
sources.rights: Link to entry and attribute editor; do not bulk copy entry text
sources.note: Each entry may aggregate sources from different periods and regional varieties. Verify the cited underlying passage.

sources.name: Gran Diccionario Náhuatl
sources.rights: Link and cite specific entry and source work; do not mirror database contents
sources.note: Contains dictionaries from different eras, regions and orthographic standards; a result is not automatically Classical Nahuatl.

sources.name: Molina, Vocabulario (1571), digitized original
sources.publisher: University of Kansas Libraries / Primeros Libros de las Américas
sources.rights: The library marks this historical work as free of known copyright restrictions; attribute transcription and edition
sources.note: Original historical spellings should be transcribed directly from the relevant page before claiming attestation.

sources.name: Amoxcalli — Classical Nahuatl Lexicon
sources.publisher: Independent lexicon based on Rémi Siméon (1885) and other collections
sources.rights: Link and attribute original sources; identify machine-translated glosses
sources.note: Machine translations and aggregate lexical entries require independent review; do not use them as stand-alone manuscript evidence.

sources.name: Launey, An Introduction to Classical Nahuatl
sources.rights: Limited-preview copyrighted academic text; link and cite page only
sources.note: Chapters 1 and 3 document the subject and object prefix paradigm. Applying the pattern to a specific verb remains a rule-derived hypothesis.

sources.name: Early Nahuatl Library
sources.publisher: Wired Humanities Projects, University of Oregon; Stephanie Wood, ed.
sources.kind: 16th–19th century Nahuatl manuscript transcriptions (specific document dated mid-16th century)
sources.rights: Site and scholarly transcription have their own rights; quote no extensive transcription without permission; link to source with line/section instead.
sources.note: For the Coyoacan example, consult AGN Tierras 1735, exp. 2 / Beyond the Codices Doc. 26, transcribed/translated by Lockhart. Editorial intro and primary transcription are not interchangeable.

sources.name: San Lucas 1833, Nahuatl Gospel of Luke
sources.publisher: Mariano Paz y Sánchez; London: Samuel Bagster / BFBS (1833). MissionAssist digital edition at Bible.com
sources.kind: 19th-century Puebla-area Nahuatl Bible translation, **not** 16th-century central Mexican corpus
sources.rights: Link to verse and identifying spelling only; the host digital edition may have additional terms. Do not bulk ingest chapters.
sources.note: Cambridge University Library notes a Puebla-area variety in ca.1830 translation. Distinguish from the early colonial document language and source editions.
